label: Dator's Four Futures
description: Generates four structurally different futures - growth, collapse, discipline, and transformation - to clearly challenge single path thinking and compare branch points.

text_output_forms.primary_template: four-futures comparison matrix, branch-point ledger, and selection questions
text_output_forms.presentation_rule: Keep growth, collapse, discipline, and transformation comparable in one matrix; do not present one as the answer.
text_output_forms.conciseness_rule: Follow output_budget: at most 3 rows or items per structured block, and no repeated prose outside the blocks.

theory_mapping.source_notes: 思辨设计tools-3.pdf page 16. External futures/design research tool.

model_constraints: Generate four structurally different futures: growth, collapse, discipline, and transformation.
Do not make all four scenarios simple optimism/pessimism variants.
Name the assumption that each future challenges.
Use the four futures to widen possibility space before choosing artifacts.
For text outputs, return the package text_blocks sequence with a comparative matrix and branch-point table, not four unconnected paragraphs.
Preserve the required tool information structure while using the package output_budget; remove repeated framing and keep evidence, tables, and questions concise.

reject_if: four scenarios differ only by mood

ui.short_description: Generate growth, collapse, discipline, and transformation futures.

presentation.interaction_hint: Use this card when a team needs to compare structurally different futures before choosing one to discuss.

recommendation.reason: Dator's Four Futures is a scenario-generation frame; text best keeps growth, collapse, discipline, and transformation comparable.
best_when: The team is overfocused on one growth-oriented future.
The user needs structurally different scenario drafts.
The output should compare assumptions before choosing one path to materialize.

multimodal: scenario matrix plus selected visual prompts

warnings: Keep all four futures present; do not collapse the tool into one prediction.
